Guest verified by HomeToGo

We had a fantastic stay and would happily return. The apartment was spotlessly clean, modern, and had everything we needed for a relaxing holiday. The Wi-Fi and air conditioning worked perfectly throughout our stay, and the beds were incredibly comfortable. Our favourite part was the balcony overlooking the beautiful gardens – it was a lovely place to sit with a coffee in the morning or a drink in the evening, with plenty of comfortable seating. The pool area was also excellent, with crystal-clear water and a peaceful atmosphere, so we spent lots of time relaxing there. Although it’s a little further from Puerto Banús than where we usually stay, we actually enjoyed the quieter location. It was an easy walk to Puerto Banús, the beach, Nueva Andalucía and San Pedro, and taxis back in the evening were quick and inexpensive. Overall, a brilliant apartment in a peaceful setting, and we’d highly recommend it to anyone visiting Marbella.

We rented the villa for one week as a group of 16 people and had a wonderful stay. The villa offers plenty of space and, overall, matches the description very well. Located slightly outside the center and up on a hillside, the property benefits from a pleasant breeze — a real blessing in the summer heat. One of the highlights was that there were truly enough seating and lounging options for everyone, both indoors and outdoors, which is not always the case in large group accommodations. A major positive was the excellent on-site support. The local team was always available, incredibly responsive, and solved any request or issue right away — we felt really well taken care of. A supermarket is about a 10-minute walk away, although the way back is uphill. The beach can also be reached by foot in around 15 minutes. By car it’s quicker, but parking near the beach can be a bit tricky. Overall, we had a fantastic time and would definitely recommend this villa for large groups.

## Yachts, history and beauty in Marbella

### Marbella Harbour

The Marbella Harbour, popularly known as Puerto Banús **,** is considered to be the most exclusive harbour in the Málaga area. Luxurious yachts moor here surrounded by a wining and dining experience which attracts celebrities and royalty alike.

### Marbella Old Quarter

As its name suggests, the Marbella Old Quarter is the original town with many traditional buildings and narrow, winding cobbled streets. In the area you will find boutique shops, quaint art galleries, pubs and restaurants.

### Alameda Park

Located to the south of the Marbella Old Quarter is Alameda Park. This small park is a tranquil place to relax and view the many beautiful tropical plants on display. In the heart of the park is a magnificent fountain, decorated with colourful, traditional Andalusian tile-work, and decorated benches for a well-deserved break.

### Avenida del Mar

The Avenida del Mar is a pedestrian street connecting the Marbella Old Quarter and the Golden Mile beach. As you head down through the Alameda Park to the beach, you will encounter an open air art gallery displaying ten surrealistic sculptures by the Spanish artist **Salvador Dalí**.

### Iglesia Mayor de la Encarnacion

The Iglesia Mayor de la Encarnacion, or Church Of The Incarnation, is a major attraction for visitors to Marbella. Located next to the castle, the church, built in 1505, is a mixture of Renaissance, Gothic and baroque styles and is home to the Lady of Solitude statue.

- Which top landmarks you shouldn't miss in Marbella?



You definitely want to check out the Old Town, also called the Casco Antiguo, which is full of charming whitewashed buildings and narrow streets. The Plaza de los Naranjos is a beautiful square in the heart of the Old Town. And don't forget to see the iconic Marbella Church, Iglesia de la Encarnación, with its beautiful bell tower.

Marbella has a Mediterranean climate with warm, sunny summers and mild, wet winters. Expect average highs in the 80s during the summer and lows in the 50s during the winter. You'll get plenty of sunshine year-round!

- What are the best short term rentals with a pool in Marbella?

- Are there any famous stadiums or sports arenas in Marbella?

- What notable natural landmarks are near Marbella?

## Discover Marbella

Marbella is a dream destination for lovers of beaches, sunshine, and Andalusian culture. On our website, you will find around 50 different accommodations that guarantee every guest an unforgettable holiday. Over 40 holiday apartments in Marbella offer the comfort you need to relax under the Mediterranean sun or explore the treasures of this fascinating city. Discover our selection of holiday apartments in Marbella - many are located near the beach and feature pools as well as other amenities. Start your day with a coffee on your balcony overlooking the sea and then stroll through the picturesque streets of the old town to exclusive beaches filled with lively chiringuitos (beach bars). Marbella's vibrant nightlife attracts numerous visitors just like its cultural highlights do. Whether it's a romantic getaway or a family holiday: Book one of ours perfect holiday apartments in Marbella now and let yourself be enchanted by this unique seaside resort's charm.

## Marbella - In 3 days

During your three-day vacation, you can relax in a cozy apartment in Marbella. Start your journey in Marbella with a leisurely stroll through the charming old town, "Casco Antiguo." Discover the narrow, cobblestone streets, the Plaza de los Naranjos, and numerous boutiques and craft shops. Afterwards, unwind at Marbella's famous beach, swim in the clear Mediterranean Sea, and enjoy a seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant. End the evening in a tapas bar. Begin the second day with a visit to the Bonsai Museum, which houses an impressive collection of bonsai trees from around the world. Then, take a walk through the Parque de la Alameda, which invites you to linger with its exotic plants and artistic tiled benches. In the afternoon, go for a hike in the nearby Sierra Blanca mountains and enjoy the breathtaking views. Spend the evening in a traditional Andalusian restaurant. On the third day, visit the Iglesia de la Encarnación, an impressive 16th-century church. In the afternoon, explore the Museo del Grabado Español Contemporáneo, which showcases contemporary Spanish prints. To conclude, enjoy dinner in a cozy restaurant in the old town and savor authentic Andalusian cuisine. Enjoy the sun and the sea while staying in your apartment in Marbella.

## Marbella - the most important activities

### Viewpoints

The Mirador de Juanar offers a breathtaking view of the surrounding mountains, the valley, and the coast, especially at sunrise and sunset. The Mirador de la Concha provides a spectacular view of Marbella, the Mediterranean Sea, and, on clear days, even the coast of Africa. At the Mirador de los Gitanos, you can enjoy an impressive view of the Sierra Blanca and the valleys below, making it ideal for hikers and nature lovers. The Mirador Arroyo de Las Represas offers a magnificent view of the surrounding forests and waterways, particularly stunning in spring and autumn. All these viewpoints are perfect places to enjoy the beauty and tranquility of nature. An apartment in Marbella is the ideal starting point to visit the most beautiful viewpoints in the region.

### Cultural activities

At the Museo del Grabado Español Contemporáneo, visitors can admire contemporary Spanish prints and participate in workshops. The Ralli Museum offers a fascinating collection of Latin American artworks, including paintings and sculptures by artists such as Salvador Dalí and Marc Chagall, as well as thematic exhibitions and guided tours. In the Avenida del Mar Sculpture Park, art lovers can enjoy impressive outdoor sculptures by Salvador Dalí and participate in cultural events and art markets. The Teatro Ciudad de Marbella is a cultural hotspot with a variety of performances, workshops, and special programs for children, introducing them to the world of theater. An apartment in Marbella offers a wonderful opportunity to explore the local culture and history.

### Annual events

The Marbella Starlite Festival is a glamorous music and cultural event in July and August that attracts international stars and offers an unforgettable experience. The Marbella International Film Festival in October is a significant platform for independent filmmakers with film screenings, workshops, and networking events. The Feria de San Bernabé in June transforms Marbella into a colorful spectacle with parades, flamenco dances, and culinary delights to celebrate regional culture. The Marbella International Art Fair in September attracts art lovers and collectors, presents contemporary artworks, and offers a platform for creative exchange through exhibitions and art talks.

### Sport activities

Marbella is a paradise for sports enthusiasts. Golfers can play at the renowned Marbella Golf & Country Club, as well as at Los Naranjos Golf Club and La Quinta Golf & Country Club. Tennis enthusiasts will find top-notch facilities and ideal weather conditions all year round. Sailors can explore the coast from Puerto Banús, with numerous courses and charter options available. Beach volleyball fans enjoy the sporty atmosphere at the beaches of Playa de la Fontanilla and Playa del Cable. Marbella offers the perfect environment for every athlete, combining sports activities with Mediterranean flair. An apartment in Marbella is ideal for sports-loving travelers who want to explore the area.

## Rent a Holiday Home in Marbella

Renting villas in Marbella in Spain has been popular with holiday makers for many years. A holiday in Marbella means a touch of class and a chance to see some rich people at play in Puerto Banus. However, self-catering rentals in Marbella does not mean you need to take out a second mortgage. It is easy to get the chance to enjoy a little bit of luxury at a fraction of the cost when renting a villa or an apartment in the local area. You will also be spoiled for choice when it comes to the best things to see and do in Marbella.

## A Self-Catering Holiday in Marbella

It does not matter if you are traveling as a couple, or as a family, renting a holiday home in Marbella is easy. Traditionally, this is perhaps the top place in Spain where visitors have come to enjoy a holiday since the 1980's when the resort first became popular with what we now call the jet set. It is a nice area of Spain, but Marbella was, believe it or not, originally a mining town. Today, when you look at Marbella, it is hard to imagine its industrial past. It has become one of the top luxury resorts for holiday lettings in Spain. Rent an apartment in Marbella, and you may end up looking out over the most exclusive marina in Spain – Puerto Banus.

That being said, Marbella has a range of good accommodation available for rent all year around. You will find anything from top class apartments, town houses and fabulous villas. One of the advantage of renting villas in Marbella, is that there is something to see and do for everybody. The children have access to some beautiful kept beaches, and enjoying a meal out is a special experience.

## Best Things to See or Do in Marbella on Your Vacation

Although Marbella is often thought of as a playground for the rich, it has plenty of family friendly activities. The beach is perhaps the main focus for many families who visit the area, but you should not neglect some of the other sightseeing opportunities. You are not far from historical cities such as Seville, Cordoba and Granada. There are plenty of day trips available to all three cities, and you may even want to take advantage of some duty free shopping in Gibraltar.

Selwo Marina is a great place to take the kids. It has a wonderful dolphin show but you can also enjoy the sea lions. There are actually three parks which are members of the Selwo group, and when you visit the wildlife park, you can take a ride in a cable car.

For the adults, there are excellent golfing facilities in the local area, and you can tee off at any of three golf courses. The best local golf course in the Marbella area is Aloha golf club with its pretty setting with a view to the mountains. To be honest, the Aloha golf club is just as well known locally for its excellent food. Many visit just to dine and enjoy some of the superb local views of the Spanish countryside.

## Beaches in the Marbella Area

Bounty beach is close to the Marbella town center, and is perhaps the trendiest beach in the area. It is surrounded by a good selection of bars, but the atmosphere is still relaxed and very casual. A good place to come if you have young children who enjoy playing on the beach without wanting to be distracted by too many beach activities.

Playa de Rio real is only five minutes away from Bounty beach, and forms part of the Los Monteros coastline. It can get very busy during summer, but if you enjoy having the benefit of local activities such as windsurfing and banana boat rides, this is the best beach to visit close to Marbella. The restaurants in the local area tend to be expensive, so it could be a good idea to bring a packed lunch along and plenty of sunscreen.

If you are looking for golden sands and some great chiringuitos where you can get out of the midday heat, you want to check out Playa Real de Zaragoza. It is a 15 minute drive from the center of Marbella, but perfect when you fancy a day on the beach. The beach does not seem to get crowded even on busy summer days, and if you don't want to rent a parasol and sun bed, you can easily find your own spot on the beach.

In the Marbella area, you will also find three fully accessible beaches. They are excellent but the Misericordia beach is the best one. It even has facilities for the hard of hearing, and if you have a handicapped traveler in your party, this beach is worth a visit.

## Convenience and Daily Essentials in Marbella

When you want to make the mot out of your self-catering holiday in Marbella, you may want to stock up on supplies as you arrive in town. If you are looking for a budget supermarket, you will find there is a Lidl in Mijas. However, one of the best local supermarkets is Alcampo, which is located in Marbella. Price wise it may even beat Lidl, and the food is always nice and fresh. It is well stocked at all times, and you can easily do a full week's shopping in this supermarket, handy if you plan to spend your time relaxing at the pool.

If you are looking for a fine dining experience in Marbella, there are a few Michelin star restaurants around. But, if you are traveling with a family, you may not want to be spending all of your time in Michelin style restaurants. There are family restaurants in the Puerto Deportivo, and if you enjoy Spanish seafood, you should try Hermano Haro. Another restaurant worth mentioning is Hacienda Patagonia which is located one street back from the seafront in Marbella. The restaurant serves up delicious Argentian meat and is not expensive at all. It is perhaps one of the best kept dining secrets in the Marbella area.

Marbella on the Costa del Sol is worth a visit and you don't need to spend a fortune. However, it is fun to sit in the Puerto Banus marina and watch the the jet set. Perhaps a walk around the exclusive boutiques will finish the evening of nicely.

## Marbella Holiday Rentals - come to the classic sunsoaked Spanish holiday jewel of the south coast

The city of Marbella is the second most populous municipality in the province of Malaga, after the homonymous provincial capital of Malaga, and the eighth most densely inhabited city of Andalusia, meaning it is the perfect holiday location for those on the hunt for an exciting, lively and action-packed city break with lots of people to meet. It is part of the popular coastal holiday region of Costa del Sol which is visited by thousands of tourists every year who flock to its shores from all over the world for the blissfully sunny weather, golden beaches, sparkling blue Mediterranean waters and gorgeous Marbella apartments. If hot and sunny weather, long stretches of idyllic beach, heavenly blue sea waters and wonderful holiday villas sound like your idea of holiday heaven, take a look at Begi Villas - where you can tour the Istrian vineyards and taste some of the world's most delicious wines!

## Marbella Holiday Villas - come and visit the sizzling Costa del Sol

There are 27 kilometres of idyllic coastline to explore in when renting **Marbella holiday homes**, divided into 24 separate beaches, the most notable being Artola, Venus and La Fontanilla, Puerto Banús and San Pedro Alcántara, which have been awarded the blue flag award for their clean water, safe surroundings and environmentally friendly practices, and Cabopino, one of the few nudist beaches in the city, for those who are feeling daring and adventurous! Marbella is undoubtedly one of the most important tourist city destinations on the Costa del Sol and attracts tourists to its shores all year round due to its favourable warm and pleasant climate and well-developed tourist infrastructure and facilities. The city also boasts an important not to be underestimated archaeological heritage, many fascianting history museums and a packed-out cultural calender, with a wide range of events to suit every possible taste, from reggae to opera, in the many concert and performance spaces located in the city.

## Marbella Villa Rentals - relax on the golden sandy beaches in the cool sea breeze

For those looking for a little history education on their Marbella holidays, head to the old town of Marbella, where you can spot the ancient city walls and the two historical suburbs of the city, namely, the Barrio Alto and the Barrio Nuevo, whose layout has remained practically untouched since the 16th century. Take a leisurely wander around the Plaza de los Naranjos, which was built after the Christian reconquest of the city, and see if you can spot some important buildings - the town hall, built in 1568 by the Catholic Monarchs the Mayor's house, with its Gothic and Renaissance façade, Mudejar roof and fresco murals in its interior, and the Chapel of Santiago, the oldest religious building in the city, which predates the square itself.
